newsitem.title: USA: Unisource sees lower Q2 sales, EPS.
newsitem.headline: Unisource sees lower Q2 sales, EPS.

text.p: Unisource Worldwide Inc said on Wednesday that it expects its second quarter results for the period ending March 31, 1997, to fall below those from the year ago period due to lower prices for printing papers.

The company said, based on current paper pricing and market conditions, earnings could be as much as 15 to 20 cents per share below analysts' estimates of $0.36. Proforma earnings for the year ago second quarter totaled $0.41 a share, Unisource said.
Unisource said its second quarter revenues are expected to be "down slightly" from the second quarter of 1996.
Unisource was previously a division of Alco Standard Corp, which approved separating itself into IKON Office Products and Unisource last year.

These lower revenues, combined with a planned increase in expenses, are expected to result in a significant decrease in earnings compared with pro forma earnings in the prior year's second quarter, Unisource said.
The expense increases are related to the implementation of the company's information technology system and ongoing integration of its regional customer service centers, the Unisource said.

"We cannot predict our year-end results because of uncertainties as to paper pricing and market conditions," the company said in a statement. "We believe our strategy is sound and we remain confident in our ability to achieve a 15 percent annual growth rate over the long term."
Unisource's 1997 business plan assumed relatively flat paper pricing and modest increases in supply systems pricing, the company said.
The company said its cash flow will be sufficient to support its dividend and working capital requirements.
Additional funding for its acquisition program is available under existing credit facilities, Unisource said.
Unisource said it is in talks with several supply systems companies and expects to complete strategic acquisitions by the end of the year.
